# Independent audit: the surface-log / tilted-volume defect identity

Source: `candidate d9362f528596f345`, Sections 1–5.

Result: PASS, no correction. The exact checker `supporting computation verify_surface_log_tilted_defect_flux_slab_recovery.py` was rerun: 96 checks PASS. This relates the two possible unscaled defects and does not eliminate either one.

The contact-gradient identity gives the asserted UNscaled volume gradient bound, since every positive source has `|c_i|/L_i<=1/r_s` and the source weights sum to one. Mean log normalization and bounded L maxima give the volume L1 log bound. The radial Gauss–Green trace inequality then bounds the boundary logarithms, so weak compactness of their negative parts is legitimate.

For the limiting ordinary trace, the finite-plane L has bounded weak gradient. Reciprocal integrability dominates both the gradients of log(L+delta) and their differences. The logarithms converge in W1,1; the radial trace estimate makes their boundary values Cauchy in L1. The zero set is surface-null by the finite-plane zero-facet divergence argument, so the resulting trace is precisely log L a.e. This supplies the limiting Gauss–Green formula even though L may vanish at codimension-two boundary faces.

The nonnegative surface defect is obtained with continuous bounded logarithmic truncations, not from an unjustified convergence of unbounded boundary densities. Uniform plane convergence and actual normal-bundle convergence pass each truncation. The positive logarithmic part is uniformly bounded and has no defect. Moreover any normal recorded by the defect is a genuine supporting normal at its limiting boundary point, by the closed graph of the convex normal relation; it need not be an a.e. unique normal of the unweighted limiting surface measure.

The exact vector-measure identity before the limit has factor M_j: `grad log L_j dm_j=M_j sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij)c_ij rho_ij`. Its weak limit is the ordinary gradient volume measure PLUS `M sum_i c_i zeta_i`. This follows from the already retained labeled rows and does not identify the tilted row with its original-volume reweighting. Zero-weight labels vanish by the lower source-value bound and bounded slopes.

In Gauss–Green the signed boundary logarithm tends to `log L eta−b`. Subtracting the limiting ordinary formula therefore gives precisely

    −pi_*(n b)=M sum_i c_i zeta_i.

The minus sign and the factor M are correct. Smooth physical tests suffice and extend by density; no normal-dependent test on the volume defect is asserted. There is also no internal crease measure in the first weak derivative of a continuous finite-PL logarithm. The source correctly declines to split the actual surface defect label by label without further interface terms.

The radial test is strictly positive: on a labeled defect, the touching plane is zero, so `c_i.(X−g_z)=−A_i(z,g_z)`. Every such plane dominates the positive interior value L(z,g_z), while every actual defect normal has `n.(X−g_z)>=r_b`. This proves the two-sided mass comparison and the exact equivalence `b=0 iff zeta=0`, including arbitrary possible cancellations between vector gradients. It is a geometric identity, not an argument that the common value is zero.

Finally, on the truncated triangles the shrinking cut facet contributes `sqrt(2) log2` at outward normal `−(1,1)/sqrt(2)`. The coordinate sides have no additional defect by their exact logarithmic primitive. With `M=1/2`, `c_i=e^(1/2)(1,1)` and `zeta=2e^(−1/2)log2 delta_0`, both vector sides are `(log2,log2)`; the centered radial value is `(2/3)log2`. The example checks the normalization and is correctly excluded from a deepest-source or physical-minimum claim.
